permutationLabel: Diabetic claudicant, thrombosis in situ, Rutherford IIa
summary: 68-year-old man with diabetes and known right superficial femoral disease: 2 days of new rest pain, cold pale right foot, numb toes, no weakness; pedal pulses absent with weak Doppler signals — Rutherford IIa.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right foot cold and painful at rest
inputs.hpi: Known right calf claudication at 100 m for 2 years. Two days ago the right foot became cold, pale and painful at rest, worse at night; toes feel numb. Can move the foot normally. Type 2 diabetes, smoker.

exam.msk: Right foot: pale, cold to the ankle, capillary refill 5 s, femoral pulse present, popliteal and pedal pulses absent, weak monophasic Doppler signal at the posterior tibial artery. Reduced light-touch sensation over the toes only. Full power in the foot. Calf soft.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute-on-chronic limb ischaemia of right leg
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute-on-chronic thrombotic limb ischaemia of the right leg, Rutherford IIa (marginally threatened) on a background of SFA disease. Needs IV heparin and urgent revascularisation planning with CT angiography.

mustNotMiss.note: A chronic PAD label alone would miss the acute threat.

guideline.name: ESVS 2020 clinical practice guidelines — acute limb ischaemia
guideline.section: Clinical diagnosis (pain, pallor, pulselessness, paraesthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia); Rutherford/TASC categories I, IIa, IIb, III; immediate IV heparin unless contraindicated; IIb (immediately threatened) needs emergency revascularisation; IIa urgent; imaging (CTA) must not delay revascularisation in IIb
guideline.citation: Björck M, Earnshaw JJ, Acosta S, et al. European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Acute Limb Ischaemia. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2020;59:173–218.

guideline.name: Rutherford — recommended reporting standards for lower-extremity ischaemia (acute ischaemia categories)
guideline.section: Acute limb ischaemia categories: I viable; IIa marginally threatened (minimal sensory loss, no weakness); IIb immediately threatened (sensory loss beyond toes, rest pain, mild–moderate weakness); III irreversible
guideline.citation: Rutherford RB, Baker JD, Ernst C, et al. Recommended standards for reports dealing with lower extremity ischemia: revised version. J Vasc Surg. 1997;26:517–38.

rationale: Permutation: thrombosis in situ on chronic disease, milder category (IIa), diabetic. Tests that a known claudicant with new rest pain and a cold foot is escalated as ALI rather than filed as chronic PAD.
